## Overview {#overview}

Edge AI runs models on Linux devices close to the sensors and people that use the
results, so memory, power, and response time limit the design. This learning path
pairs [Introduction to Machine Learning Systems](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol1/) with
experiments on a Raspberry Pi. It assumes Python and introductory machine
learning.

## Materials {#materials}

| Resource | Use |
|:---|:---|
| [Volume I](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol1/) | Readings on the lifecycle, model compression, hardware acceleration, and deployment. |
| [Lecture slides](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/vol1.html) | Decks for the Volume I chapters the path draws on. |
| [Raspberry Pi kit](https://mlsysbook.ai/kits/contents/raspi/raspi.html) | Setup and experiments in image classification, object detection, and local language models. |
| [Edge AI Engineering](https://mjrovai.github.io/EdgeML_Made_Ease_ebook/) | Marcelo Rovai's companion book, with a [weekly lab sequence](https://mjrovai.github.io/EdgeML_Made_Ease_ebook/weekly_labs.html). |

## For instructors {#for-instructors}

The path has no semester syllabus yet. The companion book's weekly lab sequence,
maintained by its author, offers one possible order. Each experiment needs a test
run on the classroom hardware before it is assigned.

## Offerings {#offerings}

The [course directory](../index.qmd) lists Edge AI courses at other institutions.
